SUMMARY—Revises provisions governing the authority of the 
State Department of Agriculture relating to food and 
water. (BDR 51-1121) 
 
FISCAL NOTE: Effect on Local Government: No. 
 Effect on the State: Yes.

EXPLANATION – Matter in bolded italics is new; matter between brackets [omitted material] is material to be omitted. 
 
 
AN ACT relating to public safety ; transferring the authority to 
regulate and permit food establishments from the Division 
of Public and Behavioral Health of the Department of 
Health and Human Services to the State Department of 
Agriculture; transferring the authority of the State Board 
of Health to adopt, amend and enforce regulations to 
provide for the sanitary protection of water and food 
supplies to the State Department of Agriculture; repealing 
various provisions governing food establishments; 
requiring, with certain exceptions, a county to pay an 
assessment to the Department for services relating to food 
establishments; revising provisions relating to the 
purchase or use of  hemp or commodities or products 
made using hemp by certain persons who operate a food 
establishment; providing penalties; and providing other 
matters properly relating thereto. 
Legislative Counsel’s Digest: 
 Existing law provides for the permitting and re gulation of food establishments, 1 
cottage food operations and farm -to-fork events by the Division of Public and 2 
Behavioral Health of the Department of Health and Human Services and, in some 3 
instances, the local boards of health. (Chapter 446 of NRS) Sections 2-13 and 16-4 
44 of this bill transfe r the authority for the permitting and regulation of food 5 
establishments, cottage food operations and farm -to-fork events from the Division 6

to the State Department of Agriculture and the local boards of health. Section 9 7 
defines the term “food safety authority” to mean the officers and agents of the 8 
Department or the officers and agents of the local boards of health. Section 77 of 9 
this bill repeals the existing provisions of law governing food establishments. 10 
Section 74 of this bill provides that any permit issued by the Division or health 11 
authority pursuant to the repealed provisions of law shall remain effective until the 12 
expiration of the permit. Section 75 of this bill provides that any regulation adopted 13 
by a local board of health which was previously required to be approved by the 14 
State Board of Health shall be deemed approved by the Department. Sections 45-15 
50, 52-60 and 63-70 of this bill make conforming changes to internal references to 16 
reflect the transfer of authority to the Department.  17 
 Existing law authorizes the State Board of Health to adopt, amend and enforce 18 
regulations to provide for the sanitary protection of water and food s upplies. (NRS 19 
439.200) Existing law further authorizes a district board of health to adopt 20 
regulations consistent with law to provide for the sanitary protection of water and 21 
food supplies. (NRS 439.366, 439.410) Section 14 of this bill transfers the 22 
authority to adopt regulations to provide for the sanitary protection of water and 23 
food supplies from the State Board of Health to the Department. Sections 61 and 24 
62 of this bill require any regulations adopted by a district board of health relating 25 
to the sanitary protection of water and food supplies to be consistent with any 26 
regulations adopted by the Department.  27 
 Existing law requires each county to pay an assessment to the Division in an 28 
amount determined by the Division for the costs of services provided in that county 29 
by the Division, including services relating to food establishments. Existing law 30 
authorizes a county to request to carry out these services and receive an exemption 31 
from this assessment from the Interim Finance Committee. (NRS 439.4905) 32 
Section 15 of this bill  requires each county to pay an assessment for the costs of 33 
any services provided in the county by the Department relating to food 34 
establishments and authorizes a county to request to carry out these services and 35 
receive an exemption from the Interim Finan ce Committee. Section 51 of this bill 36 
authorizes the Interim Finance Committee to perform this duty during a regular or 37 
special session. Section 76 of this bill provides that any county which has already 38 
received such an exemption shall be deemed to have received an exemption from 39 
the assessment required by section 15. 40 
 Existing law authorizes a person who holds a permit to operate a food 41 
establishment and who operates a food establishment at which food is not prepared 42 
or served for immediate consumption to  purchase and use hemp or a commodity or 43 
product made using hemp to manufacture or prepare and sell, offer or display food 44 
that contains an approved hemp component at the food establishment. (NRS 45 
446.844) Section 18 provides that a person may only purchase or use hemp or a 46 
commodity or product made using hemp that the United States Food and Drug 47 
Administration has determined to be safe or generally recognized as safe for u se as 48 
an ingredient in food intended for human consumption. 49
